Hi Samantha — thanks, this is helpful context. Attached is a compact worksheet (redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx) plus a one-page CSV summary I pulled for quick viewing. High level:

- Marginal pricing: token-by-token pricing that applies the lower per-token rate only to tokens in the higher breakpoint band. Best for customers who want transparent unit economics as they grow. Example (quick):
  - 0–500M tokens: $0.00060/token
  - 500M–2B tokens: $0.00045/token
  - >2B tokens: $0.00035/token
  - If you use 700M tokens, marginal cost = (500M * 0.00060) + (200M * 0.00045) / 700M = ~$0.00054/token average

- Blended pricing: a single effective $/token applied to all tokens based on the achieved tier threshold (often used for committed, simple billing). Example: 700M tokens blended rate could be $0.00050/token (one price across volume).

- Hybrid / sliding slab: we can support a slab where prices step down at breakpoints (marginal inside bands) but include a capped true-up mechanism (e.g., if actual 12-month usage < commit by more than X%, a floor blended credit applies). This reduces volatility for finance while preserving incentives to scale.

Attached: redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (XLSX), redwood_pricing_summary.csv (CSV) — both have worked examples and a toggle between marginal, blended, and hybrid projections.

Operational notes: monthly invoices, quarterly true-up windows (can be made monthly if needed), and we expose per-route token breakdowns in the console for reconciliation.

Hi Samantha / Lauren — circling in with one worked example and an alternative structure we often recommend.

Worked example (commit = 3.6B tokens / 12 months; ramp to 500M/mo after month 4):
- Marginal bands (example): 0–500M @ $0.00060; 500M–2B @ $0.00045; >2B @ $0.00035
- Suppose annual actual = 4.2B tokens (above commit): marginal billing applies and your average $/token = weighted average of each band. If actual < commit, true-up applies on the shortfall at the blended floor price defined in the SOW.

Hybrid (sliding slab) we propose for pilots:
- Monthly billing uses marginal inside bands for transparency.
- Quarterly true-up with a floor blended cap: if actual usage < 85% of committed volume for the quarter, the shortfall is billed at a floor blended rate equal to the weighted average price of the committed volume (protects revenue). Cap the true-up to 15% of committed value per quarter and 30% annually.

Why this helps: finance avoids extreme retroactive charges; engineering retains growth incentive. Attached in the worksheet are two scenarios: (A) conservative adoption (75% of commit) and (B) on-track adoption (110% of commit). Both have line items for credits and an optional one-time onboarding credit to offset early churn risk.

Let me know if you want the spreadsheet adjusted to the exact token distribution per month — happy to model.
